: Mr. Abhishek Singh, Advocate.

For the State : Mr. Shailendra Kumar Tiwari, A.P.P.
---------
th Order No. 06/Dated: 13 September, 2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Jamtara Cyber Crime P.S. Case No. 06 of 2024,
registered under Sections 414, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120(B) of the I.P.C. and under Section 66(B)
(C) (D) of the I.T. Act, the petitioner has moved to this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Jamtara Cyber Crime P.S. Case No. 06 of 2024
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the FIR, allegation is that a secret informant was received by informant that some persons were committing Cyber Crime.
Upon raid, all persons tried to flee, but on chase, two persons were apprehended and they disclosed the name of other accused persons.

Upon search, in huge quantity,
mobile phones along with SIM cards were recovered and seized.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case, only on the basis of confessional statement of the co-accused which has no evidentiary value in the eye of law.
Petitioner was not arrested in this case and no incriminated articles has been recovered from the house of the petitioner in connection of this case.

Petitioner undertakes to cooperate with the investigation of the case and abide by all terms and conditions, as imposed by this Court, in the event of granting Page 1|2 anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

On the other hand, learned SPl.P.P appearing for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and submitted that petitioner has two criminal antecedents of the same offences and investigation against the petitioner is still going on.
There are sufficient materials showing involvement of the petitioner in the alleged offence.
Hence, he does not deserve anticipation bail to the petitioner.

Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation materials showing involvement of the present petitioner in alleged Cyber Crime and investigation against the petitioner is still going on, he has also criminal antecedent of same offences as mentioned in the report submitted by the learned Spl.P.P., being Cyber Crime P.S. Case No. 31 of 2023 dated 31.05.2023 under Section 414, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120(B) of the I.P.C. and under Section 66(B)
(C) (D) of the I.T. Act.

entities.text: Cyber Crime P.S. Case No. 31 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It also appears that other co- accused was granted anticipatory bail by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, who has no criminal antecedent.
Hence, case of the petitioner stands different footing.
I am not inclined to extend the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Accordingly, the prayer of anticipatory bail of petitioner is rejected.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Simran/ Page 2|2 Nijamuddin Ansari @ Afroz Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand ..... Opp. Party on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140936424/
